A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same truncated polynomial classifier (TPC) research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments on WildGuardMix and BeaverTails, cascade evaluations, feature attribution and multiple training and computational ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds cross-dataset evaluations, external LLM monitor comparisons and model-family layer sweeps.

M1.justification: The mean-pooled inputs, polynomial architecture, symmetric CP factorization, progressive training loss and cascading algorithm remain unchanged. The corrected confidence-condition prose agrees with the already-correct Algorithm 1 in v1; input-driven terminology and transposed matrix conventions do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained WildGuardMix and BeaverTails evaluations, v3 tests WildGuardMix-trained monitors on HarmBench, ToxicChat and OpenAI-moderation (Appendix F.2). These introduce substantial coverage of different textual styles, class distributions and harm-labeling policies.

E2.justification: v1 compares TPCs with linear, bilinear, MLP and early-exit MLP probes. v3 retains these comparisons and adds evaluated external monitors: gpt-4o-mini, claude-3-haiku, o3-mini, Llama-Guard-3-8B and shieldgemma-2b (Table 4).

E3.justification: The original splits and degree-5, rank-64 setup remain. Added protocols include cross-dataset testing with accuracy, precision, recall and false rejection rate; prompted external-monitor evaluation; and six-layer sweeps on Llama-3.2-1B/3B and Llama-3.1-8B. Table 1 also introduces a validation-selected layer summary of existing results, without establishing reruns.

E4.justification: Appendix F.2 adds distribution-shift tests and selected false-positive cases examining incompatible harm-labeling policies. Appendix F.4 adds systematic model-size and layer sensitivity analyses. The original calibration, progressive-training, latency, rank, maximum-degree and symmetry analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-seed averages for the main comparisons and seed-0 cascade experiments. The added layer sweeps follow the existing five-seed averaging practice; no new statistical uncertainty estimation, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: The original plotted results and ablations are retained, while Tables 3–7 add substantial transfer, external-monitor and layer-wise results. For example, ToxicChat F1 is 57.66 for fifth-order TPC, 52.97 for EE-MLP and 46.27 for the linear probe. These are newly reported evaluations, not same-setting improvements over v1; Table 1 summarizes existing full-depth results.

T1.justification: The polynomial definitions, progressive loss, feature-attribution derivation and parameter/FLOP analyses remain mathematically equivalent. Factor-matrix transpositions and corresponding index changes revise notation; no substantive theory, assumption or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions remain the same. The introduction narrows the novelty framing by acknowledging existing probe-to-LLM cascades, replacing v1's suggestion that dynamic computation had yet to bring comparable flexibility to safety monitoring.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of transfer errors through differing harm policies, qualifications about untuned external monitors and speculative model sizes, and explanations of layer-selection sensitivity. The conclusion newly acknowledges nonmonotonic performance with additional compute and the need for layer search, while retaining the earlier small-data and interpretability limitations.

D1.justification: v3 supplies the external-monitor system prompt and model access references, transfer-dataset selection details, and an explicit shared classification threshold of 0.5. The original code link, training grids, optimizer, hardware and epoch budgets remain; the new reproducibility statement mostly points to existing information.

R1.justification: A new Cascades & ensembles discussion substantially expands positioning, especially relative to McKenzie, Cunningham and Hua and earlier cascade literature. It distinguishes TPCs from probe-to-external-LLM pipelines and explains their possible complementarity. References also expand to support the new datasets and monitor comparisons.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section order are retained. Local revisions clarify input-level monitoring, correct the cascade explanation and harmonize notation. v3 separates static and dynamic results discussion and adds ethics, reproducibility and LLM-usage disclosures, alongside the new appendix subsections.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the result displays with the main-text static summary (Table 1), transfer table and plots (Table 3/Figure 7), external-monitor comparison (Table 4), and layer-sweep Tables 5–7. It also adds boxed examples and a system prompt. Earlier figures are largely retained and renumbered rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the paper by addressing v1's limited evidence about cross-dataset transfer and layer selection, while correcting an important gap in positioning against existing monitoring cascades. The new analyses expose labeling-policy mismatch and layer sensitivity, and the expanded limitations better qualify applicability. External-LLM comparisons carry less weight because tuning is unmatched and some parameter counts are speculative, but the broader evidence and clearer boundaries provide a substantial net improvement.
